title: Hierarchical scope fabric and permission matrix for RBAC v2
creator: Asha Kapoor
description: Objective: Define the canonical role model for RBAC v2 that maps SSO group claims and admin controls into a hierarchical resource model and scope-based permission fabric. The goal is to support least-privilege bindings across Org -> Environment -> Workspace -> Model -> Endpoint -> Route, enable fine-grained delegation, and integrate with audit logging and SSO/SAML attribute mappings. This ticket captures proposed data model, enforcement placement, migration strategy from RBAC v1, and operational controls (break-glass, emergency admin, ephemeral roles).
design_notes:
High-level design summary:

1) Resource hierarchy: we model resources with stable canonical types and parent pointers. Top-down example: Organization (org) -> Environment (env) -> Workspace -> Project -> Model -> Endpoint -> Route. Each resource has an immutable resource_id, resource_type, and tenant_key (org_id) to make queries multi-tenant safe.

2) Scope tokens: Policies assign role bindings to (principal, resource_scope, role). Resource_scope is a path prefix (e.g., org:123, org:123/env:prod, org:123/workspace:xyz). We will permit both prefix scopes and explicit single-resource scopes.

3) Role shape: Roles are named sets of permission atoms. Permission atoms are low-level verbs + resource_type (e.g., read:model, write:endpoint, invoke:route, admin:workspace). Roles support parameterized constraints (timebox, IP allowlist).

4) Permission evaluation: Runtime evaluates effective permissions by traversing the resource path from most-specific (route) up to org. Deny overrides and explicit denies are supported for emergency revocations. Caching layer (short TTL) at the API gateway will store effective permissions for (principal, resource_id) to avoid round-trips on hot paths.

5) SSO/SAML mapping: Identity provider group claims map to role bindings via an intermediate Group Binding table. We support mapping expressions (regex) and attribute-based bindings (eg. saml:department -> role:developer scoped to the org in the assertion). Group mappings are audited on sync.

6) Audit logging: Every permission change, role bind/unbind, effective-eval failure, and break-glass usage is emitted to audit streams (Kafka) with a consistent schema: event_id, timestamp, actor, action, resource_scope, outcome, context. Default retention 90 days; export hooks to SIEM provided.

7) Admin controls: Support for ephemeral elevation (time-limited admin role), emergency 'break-glass' admin with mandatory justification which creates an immutable audit event and triggers review workflow. Role separation enforced for sensitive actions (e.g., approving production model rollout requires two distinct reviewers).
permission_matrix:
Sample permission matrix (illustrative):

ROLE                     | read:model | write:model | invoke:endpoint | manage:workspace | audit:read | admin
-------------------------|------------|-------------|-----------------|------------------|-----------|-------
model-viewer             |   allow    |    deny     |      deny       |      deny        |    deny   |  deny
model-editor             |   allow    |   allow     |      deny       |      deny        |    deny   |  deny
endpoint-invoker         |   allow    |    deny     |     allow       |      deny        |    deny   |  deny
workspace-admin          |   allow    |   allow     |     allow       |     allow        |   allow   |  deny
org-admin                |   allow    |   allow     |     allow       |     allow        |   allow   |  allow

Notes: permission atoms are normalized (noun:verb) and stored as strings (eg. "model:read"). Roles are versioned; changes create audit events.
acceptance_criteria:
- Data model defined and reviewed: tables/indices for role, binding, resource, group_mapping, deny_entries, and audit_event.
- Design doc approved by Security and Platform leads.
- Prototype policy evaluation library (Go) that accepts a principal, resource_id, and desired action and returns allow/deny within 10ms cold (benchmarked) and 1ms warm with cache.
- Migration plan from RBAC v1: export existing role bindings, heuristic mapping to new roles, test import in staging, and roll-forward/rollback scripts.
- Audit events emitted for role changes and break-glass actions; sample consumer verifies events land in Kafka.
- SSO mapping patterns documented with at least one SAML IdP mapping example.
- Admin controls: UI and CLI flows for ephemeral elevation and mandatory justification documented and tested.

decisions:
Adopted decisions so far:
- Enforcement point: API gateway + runtime library. Gateway performs quick allow/deny via cached effective permissions; runtime re-checks for high-risk operations.
- Storage: authoritative bindings stored in Postgres (single primary per region) with change events emitted to Kafka for downstream caches.
- Caching: short TTL (30s) with optimistic refresh.
- Deny semantics: explicit deny wins; denies are sparse and meant for emergency revocation.
- Versioning: roles are immutable once published; updates create new role version and binding migration tools.

Open questions:
- Do we support attribute-based access control (ABAC) expressions in v1 of RBAC v2, or defer to role templates? (Tradeoff: ABAC is powerful but complicates eval performance and caching.)
- Exact retention period for audit logs (default 90 days vs configurable per org).
